review.method: acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the production baseline report over that installation, rustc and Cargo.lock; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The consumer trace is cs_content::catalog::baseline::retail_baseline + baseline_report_json, the same functions `cs-inspect catalog --cs-path` writes. Each row's identity is the resolved .mpg file's own install_file_key and its span is the file's whole extent with the file's own digest; the names come from the PLAYAVI actions of the fmv.zrd member of ZBD/zrdr.zbd, located by production container discovery and decoded by the production decode_zrd. This stage reads no other source: the raw scan behind that measurement never saw the zlib-compressed members of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof, which a review scan of 2026-10-12 read with the production reader and found naming more videos - see the first LIMITATION below and docs/findings/2026-10-12-f14-d-video-collection.md. LIMITATION: Seven inventoried .mpg files (chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg, crimflag.mpg, final.mpg) no PLAYAVI action reaches, so they are counted under the collection's `unnamed_video_file` gap and have no row. They are not unnamed everywhere: a review scan of 2026-10-12 decompressed both retail ROF containers with the production reader and found ASSETS/LAYOUT.CSV of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof spelling CrimFlag.MPG five times and Final.MPG once in MOVIE records, and ASSETS/SCRIPTS/CAMPAIGNINTRO.SCRIPT constructing the chapter name as "chap" conv$(FC) ".mpg" - this stage reads neither source, so no row is minted from them. Affected content: crimflag.mpg, final.mpg and chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg.
